cards.explanation: The answer is Bethsaida, friends. Mark says Jesus made His disciples get into the boat and go on ahead of Him to Bethsaida, while He dismissed the crowd (Mark 6:45). The boat had a heading before it ever left the shore. That's more planning than I did for my last batch, and I had a recipe card.

The answer is True. Mark says Jesus made His disciples get into the boat and go on ahead of Him, "…while He dismissed the crowd." (Mark 6:45). So they go first, and He stays behind on land. I've sent a batch ahead of me to the cooling rack plenty of times, but never with this much on the line.

The answer is pray, friends. Mark says that after bidding them farewell, Jesus "…went up on the mountain to pray." (Mark 6:46). Crowd gone, boat gone, and He heads up to pray. I think that's a good reminder to have a quiet place of your own, even if mine is the pantry.

The wind is against them, friends. Mark says Jesus "…could see that the disciples were straining to row, because the wind was against them." (Mark 6:48). The wind is pushing one way and they're pulling the other. I get tired just stirring a heavy batch, so I feel for them.

The word is walking, friends! Mark says Jesus went out to them "…walking on the sea." (Mark 6:48). Not sailing, not swimming. I can barely walk across my kitchen without my base sliding, so this stops me cold.

The word is ghost, friends. Mark says that when they saw Him walking on the sea, "…they cried out, thinking He was a ghost…" (Mark 6:49). Think about it from their seat in the boat. A figure on the water in the dark is going to get a loud reaction from anybody, and I'd have yelled too.

The answer is False, friends. Mark says "…they all saw Him and were terrified." (Mark 6:50). Nobody had to say "did you see that?" because everyone in the boat already had. If it were just one person, they might have blamed the dark. With everybody seeing it, that excuse is gone.

Jesus tells them it's Him, so don't be afraid, friends. He says, "Take courage! It is I. Do not be afraid." (Mark 6:50). Mark says He spoke up at once. Hearing a voice you know right when you're scared is a gift.
The answer is False, friends. Mark says Jesus climbed into the boat with them, "…and the wind died down." (Mark 6:51). After all that straining, the wind dies down instead of picking up.

The answer is the loaves, friends. Mark says the disciples were utterly astounded, "…for they had not understood about the loaves…" (Mark 6:52). That points back to the feeding of the crowd just before this (Mark 6:41-44). Mark names the loaves as the thing they hadn't understood.

The answer is True, friends. Mark says the disciples had not understood about the loaves, "…but their hearts had been hardened." (Mark 6:52). It's a plain, honest line about these men. I think it's a good reminder that even people who walked with Jesus had things to learn.

The answer is True, friends. Mark says that "As soon as they got out of the boat, the people recognized Jesus" (Mark 6:54). There's no waiting around and no wondering who He was. They knew Him right away.

The answer is the sick on mats, friends. Mark says the people "…ran through that whole region, carrying the sick on mats to wherever they heard He was." (Mark 6:55). They carried people who needed help straight to Jesus. That's a lot of running and a lot of carrying.

The answer is the fringe of His cloak, friends. They begged Him "…just to let them touch the fringe of His cloak." (Mark 6:56). Just the edge, nothing more. And Mark says all who touched Him were healed.
The answer is False, friends. Mark says, "And all who touched Him were healed." (Mark 6:56). Not some, not most, but all. Villages, towns and countrysides, and that word covers them all.
